question: What type of organism causes gonorrhea?
explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a Gram-negative diplococcus bacterium that infects mucosal membranes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h1)

question: How does a baby usually contract gonorrhea from an infected mother?

options.B: Via airborne droplets in the nursery ward
options.C: Across the placenta during early pregnancy
options.D: During passage through the birth canal

explanation: The infant is exposed to the bacteria directly when passing through an infected maternal cervix and vagina during delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which symptom is most typical of gonococcal cervicitis in women?

options.A: Hard painless ulcer on the vulva
options.B: Lower abdominal rash with small fluid blisters
options.C: Intense itching with thick white cheese discharge

explanation: Gonococcal infection causes localized inflammation with a characteristic pus-filled cervical discharge. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant woman tests positive for gonorrhea during routine booking but reports no physical discomfort. What does this clinical picture suggest?

options.A: The laboratory result is a false positive due to normal pregnancy flora.
options.B: She only needs partner notification without taking any antibiotics.
options.C: She has an asymptomatic infection that still requires full treatment.
options.D: Her immune system has successfully cleared the bacteria naturally.

explanation: Many women harbor the infection without symptoms, but treatment is vital to prevent severe pregnancy and neonatal complications. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which laboratory method is widely used as a primary diagnostic tool to identify Neisseria gonorrhoeae from an endocervical swab?
explanation: A Gram stain allows the midwife or lab technician to visualize the characteristic Gram-negative diplococci under a microscope. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is routine antenatal screening for sexually transmitted infections recommended during the first booking visit?

options.A: To check if the placenta is attached low in the uterine cavity
options.B: To detect hidden infections early and prevent ascending complications
options.C: To confirm the mother's blood group and rhesus compatibility
options.D: To measure the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: Early detection allows prompt treatment before the infection can ascend to the upper reproductive tract and harm the pregnancy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary antibiotic combination recommended for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea?
explanation: Standard protocols combine an injectable cephalosporin with an oral macrolide to ensure effective clearance and cover chlamydial coinfection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h4)

question: A woman receives treatment for gonorrhea at the antenatal clinic. What crucial step must the midwife take regarding her partner?

options.A: Refer the partner exclusively to a general surgical outpatient clinic.
options.B: Advise the partner to wait for severe symptoms to appear.
options.C: Treat the partner simultaneously to prevent reinfection.
options.D: Tell the partner to use condoms without needing any medication.

explanation: Simultaneous partner treatment is essential to eliminate the reservoir of infection and prevent the woman from being infected again. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the name of the severe eye infection a newborn can contract from an infected birth canal?
explanation: Ophthalmia neonatorum is a severe form of conjunctivitis acquired by the newborn during passage through a birth canal infected with gonorrhea or chlamydia. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which maternal complication is directly linked to ascending gonococcal infection in the reproductive tract?
explanation: When bacteria ascend from the cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes, it results in Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is partner notification considered a key component of gonorrhea management?

options.A: It breaks the transmission chain by treating hidden reservoirs of infection.
options.B: It proves whether the pregnant woman was faithful to her partner.
options.C: It allows the hospital to collect extra consultation fees from families.
options.D: It serves as a legal punishment for individuals who break marital vows.

explanation: Treating all exposed sexual partners stops ongoing transmission and protects the index patient from getting reinfected. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h6)

question: A patient is afraid to tell her husband about her gonorrhea diagnosis because she fears abandonment. What is the most appropriate initial midwifery action?

options.A: Refuse to treat her until she brings her husband to the clinic forcefully.
options.B: Provide confidential counseling and offer assisted partner notification support.
options.C: Report her case immediately to the local community leaders without consent.
options.D: Tell her to hide the diagnosis and take the medications secretly.

explanation: Empathetic counseling helps address her fears while finding a safe, confidential way to ensure her partner receives treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h6)
